niche.habitat: Verrin's Ring Shear-Lanes (1.4–1.6 Rv), preferring density waves and resonance edges where orbital shear is highest.
niche.diet: Water ice, hydrogen peroxide frost, grazers, reaction-mass exhaust plumes.
niche.active: Continuous diurnal activity; hunting peaks during Kessler cascade events when debris density spikes.

body: Asymmetric body: central clathrate-brain core protected by 1 mm skin; magenta-hinged reflective sail on port side for radiation pressure; starboard cluster of sublimation nozzles; shifted-amber photoreceptor array for Doppler sensing; fine debris-tracking filaments extendable from flanks.

links: Phasing requires knowing prey's orbital period
Period shifts reflected light frequency via Doppler effect
Eyes evolved shifted-amber photoreceptors to read spectral shift

skill.effect: The creature tracks the prey's orbit and anticipates where it will move next. Aiming at that predicted path makes strikes land with remarkable accuracy.

chains.weakness: Blind to optical phasing during eclipse; sensors rely on reflected light.
observe: Amber eyes glow with shifted spectrum when targeting
Tracking movements anticipate prey's future position
Lock beam points ahead of prey velocity vector

journal.en: It doesn't see where you are; it sees where you'll be.

plausibility.summary: Keep the predictive skill but change the sense: an amber (585 nm) star-and-ring tracker that measures prey angular displacement across successive sightings and eclipse clocks (F8, F12, F14) to fit an orbit. Drop the shifted-spectrum glow and lock beam; show anticipation instead. A literal spectral shift would need a narrow-band emitter this canon does not supply.
fixes: Keep the predictive skill but change the sense: an amber (585 nm) star-and-ring tracker that measures prey angular displacement across successive sightings and eclipse clocks (F8, F12, F14) to fit an orbit. Drop the shifted-spectrum glow and lock beam; show anticipation instead. A literal spectral shift would need a narrow-band emitter this canon does not supply.

analogues.organism: A dragonfly intercepting another fly by angular image motion and time-to-contact, not by colour. CF-FM bats compensate Doppler shift in echolocation, but that works because they emit a narrow-band call, which reflected sunlight is not.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Delta-v requires ejected mass for orbit changes
Mass must be recovered from environment
Catalyst bladders evolved to maximize exhaust velocity

skill.effect: The creature ignites chemical bladders to propel itself swiftly through the void. It can shift its trajectory to cut across the battlefield and reposition near targets.

chains.weakness: High peroxide use risks internal poisoning; 10% chance of self-damage if burn exceeds capacity.
observe: Nozzle clusters vent white gas with visible heat haze
Body color deepens with peroxide load
Mass gauge drops visibly with each maneuver

journal.en: It eats poison to buy speed.

plausibility.summary: Line each bladder with a peroxide-impermeable clathrate or ceramic membrane separate from the 1 mm pressure skin, feed ring ice in as expendable mass, and vent a cold collimated ice-vapour jet through the starboard nozzles. Replace 'white gas with visible heat haze' with 'a brief frosty sparkle as grains catch starlight'. Leave any self-poisoning chance to the game numbers, not the lore.

analogues.organism: Bombardier beetle (Brachinus) stores hydrogen peroxide and catalytically decomposes it into a hot defensive spray; hydrogen-peroxide monopropellant thrusters are flown on spacecraft.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Thrust can be harvested for free altitude gain
Hinge allows sail to catch radiation without blocking nozzles
Hinged sail evolved to balance lift and thrust vectoring

skill.effect: Uses radiation pressure to gain 0.5 altitude without mass cost. Reduces energy cost of outbound transfers.

chains.weakness: Sail blocks retro-thrust; cannot burn inward while sail is active.
observe: Magenta sail catches starlight and shimmers
Sail hinge clicks when adjusting angle
Outward spiral path visible during idle drift

journal.en: The star pushes it up; gravity pays the debt.

plausibility.summary: Make the sail a micron-thick radiation-toughened organic film on a light frame, not the pressure skin; gimbal the hinge through the centre of mass or add counter-rotating ballast nozzles. Let a small magenta pigment patch harvest F21 photosynthesis at the cost of a slight thrust penalty. Keep the outward-only spiral, the eclipse downtime and the journal line.
fixes: Make the sail a micron-thick radiation-toughened organic film on a light frame, not the pressure skin; gimbal the hinge through the centre of mass or add counter-rotating ballast nozzles. analogues.organism: Solar sails such as IKAROS and NanoSail-D climb with photon pressure and no propellant; ring grains feel the related Poynting-Robertson effect.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Kessler cascade creates chaotic debris field
Debris forces prey to expend reaction mass to survive
Reaction mass exhaust plumes reveal prey position
Filaments evolved to detect and track exhaust plumes

skill.effect: Amidst floating wreckage, the creature senses frantic escape attempts and tracks them effortlessly. It easily secures fleeing prey and exposes those trying to hide.

chains.weakness: Filaments can snag on large debris fragments; movement restricted in dense debris.
observe: Filaments extend into debris cloud like sensory hairs
Predator ignores open ice to focus on debris lanes

journal.en: In the storm of broken ice, the predator watches the sparks.

plausibility.summary: Describe the filaments as short-range whiskers that vibrate or taste when plume grains strike them, useful in the last metres of an intercept, and as impact hazards in dense debris. Change the secret from 'triggers a Kessler cascade' to 'kicks loose frost into a crossing orbit to flush grazers', preserving the chaos-hunting fun without breaking the energy budget.

analogues.organism: Spider trichobothria and insect antennae sense airflow and particles by direct mechanical interception; spacecraft dust detectors register single grain impacts by ionisation.

changelog.what: re-review: the referee had failed (Cursor composer-2.5 unavailable on the Free plan) and every chain defaulted to 6/fixable; verdicts redone with a working referee

temperament: Calculating patience broken by explosive action during debris events.
secrets: Can trigger micro-cascades by venting superheated gas onto slow-moving ice chunks to create cover and flush prey.
Sail pigment is magenta bacteriorhodopsin, allowing limited photosynthesis during the sail's outward drift.
moments: The ring goes dark as a cascade erupts; ice shards scream past. The Cerradora folds its sail, vents a controlled plume of white gas, and dives into the chaos where the grazers' panicked thrusts betray them. It emerges only when the debris clears, heavy with the bloated form of a grazer caught in the shear.

journal.en: It lives in the gaps between orbits.
A shadow that moves by breaking physics.
The Kessler storm is its hunting ground.
It waits for the universe to break so it can strike.
